result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers side with the dispatchers and treat the double-assignment as a system problem to fix with atomic server-side assignment and live status. B goes further on keeping work fast (one-key templates, remembering the last choice, a keyboard-only flow) and offers undo plus a logged override at the moment of assignment. It also acknowledges the GM's goal more fully. A is a little tighter and adds a sensible database constraint, but its fast-path advice is thin. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers side with the dispatchers and treat the double-assignments as a problem to fix inside the system rather than with a dialog. A is more concrete about keeping entry fast: one-key templates, remembering the last value per field, and keyboard-only entry. It also handles conflicts at the point of assignment, with busy trucks shown greyed out alongside their current job, a logged override, and an undo after assigning. B is a bit tighter and adds a database-level guard and a plan to investigate the two incidents, but it says less about the fast path and offers no undo.
